name: Petrarch, First Modern Individual
summary: Francesco Petrarch, crowned with laurel on the Capitoline Hill in Rome (1341), articulates a new relationship with classical antiquity and a new emphasis on individual self-expression. His Italian sonnets (the Canzoniere) establish the Petrarchan sonnet form; his Latin correspondence recreates classical epistolary style; his classification of medieval history as 'dark ages' between Rome and the Renaissance creates the periodization that shapes all subsequent European historiography.

_quarry.structural_significance: Petrarch is often called the 'first Renaissance man', not because he was born different from medieval men but because he expressed a distinctive historical consciousness: the sense that classical antiquity was a separate, superior civilization that could be consciously recovered; this periodization (antiquity - dark ages - modern recovery) is the master narrative of Western cultural history; Petrarch's individual self-expression in the vernacular and Latin inaugurates the Renaissance literary program
